sermon.title: 2012 Church Servants Two 0520
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer continues through 1 Corinthians 16 with the devoted leaders, the ones who serve behind the scenes and refresh others. He teaches that it matters who you follow, that unity and music in worship are tied to God’s presence, and that “Anathema” in verse 22 is about not loving the Lord Jesus Christ. He closes by saying that loving Jesus means keeping his commandments and learning how to treat other people, and that making Jesus Lord of your life keeps false leaders from leading you astray.

Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: he cites “Genesis 7” just before “Genesis 11:6” (the passage with “the people are one” is Genesis 11:6), and the caption for the reference at about 22:00 is not clear (marked [unclear]); the words he reads match Galatians 1:8. He says “Isaiah 9:16” after reading words that are Isaiah 3:12 (“those who lead you cause you to err”); both are shown. He uses King James wording (“pastors” in Jeremiah 3:15 and 12:10, “Anathema Maranatha” in 1 Corinthians 16:22), where the NKJV reads “shepherds,” “rulers” and “accursed. O Lord, come!”; his words are unchanged and the NKJV is shown separately. Caption errors for some names were corrected where the meaning was clear (“Stephanas,” “Apollos,” “Fortunatus,” “Moroni,” “anathema”). He names public figures and makes claims about other religions, homosexuality, healing, prosperity and helping the poor; those are his words, not verified by this site. “[Unclear]” marks 12 spots where the captions were not clear: a place name and a name in the reading of 1 Corinthians 16 (about 1:16 and 2:33), several words in his story about the couple who helped him (about 4:37–6:00), a word in the singing section (about 17:36), the reference at about 22:00 ([unclear] 1:8), a word in the prosperity section (about 26:28) and four words in the healing illustration (about 27:28–28:30).

chunks.section_question: What does it mean to be alert and stand fast in the faith?
chunks.short_answer: He tells the congregation “you are to … be alert,” not just to come and wait for the minister, and to “stand fast in the faith.” He says the faith is “The Scriptures, in Jesus Christ,” and urges “Have the courage of your convictions. Have the guts to stand up for what the Scriptures say.”
chunks.text: Now he goes into the attendees, the members, and devoted leaders. A different area of leadership. We had the young leader, we had the skilled leader, and now we got devoted leaders. And he talks to the congregation and says, “Be alert.” Congregation, you are to what? Be alert. You’re not supposed to come just to wait for the minister to get you into the third heaven and all that. You’re to come in alert. Hallelujah. You’re supposed to live on Monday alert, wide awake. “Stand fast in the faith.” That’s your job, to stand fast in the faith. What faith? The Scriptures, in Jesus Christ. Amen. Don’t be swaying, don’t be swerving. “Be brave,” and “be strong.” Have the courage of your convictions. Have the guts to stand up for what the Scriptures say. The Bible says homosexuality is wrong. Then have the guts to stand up and say, “Jesus and the Bible says this is wrong. I don’t care what Obama says, Bush says, Oprah says, or anybody else. Jesus said it’s wrong, the apostles said it’s wrong. By golly, it’s wrong.”

chunks.section_question: Who are the devoted leaders in 1 Corinthians 16, and what do they do?
chunks.short_answer: He says they are not a skilled minister, an apostle with signs and wonders, or a young minister, but “just devoted ministers” who are “addicted to ministry.” He says “Every church needs them,” and he lists cleaning the church, doing the books, mowing the lawn, visiting the sick and inviting people to their homes. He explains that “refresh” means “you relieve someone of the burden, you refresh them.”
chunks.text:
See, have courage to stand up for truth. Amen. “Let all that you do be done with love.” Love, not works, no harm. “I urge you, brethren,” talking to the church, you know, “the household of Stephanas, the first fruits of [unclear], that they have devoted themselves to the ministry of the saints.” They’re not Apollos, a skilled minister. They’re not the apostles that he talked about earlier with signs and wonders and so forth. They’re not a young minister. They’re just devoted ministers. They’re committed. One definition of the word is they’re addicted. They’re addicted to ministry, that they can’t do without it. How many would like to have that kind of desire in your heart, where you miss the church when you’re gone, even for a good reason, because you’re addicted to it?

Hallelujah. These are devoted. They’re committed leaders. Every church needs them and every church should have them. And he tells the congregation to submit to such, “and all who work and labor with us.” See, and then he gives two others: Fortunatus, [unclear]. Yeah. Uh, “refreshed.” See, he said they refreshed me, they supplied what was lacking. It’s like being out plowing the field, you know, and somebody, your wife, comes and brings you a nice cold glass of lemonade. Whoa, refreshes you, and you can get your strength and keep going. Or one of your sons comes out and takes the plow: “Dad, go sit under the tree, I’ll plow for a while.” That would be unique in our homes, wouldn’t it? They can’t even make their bed, let alone plow a field.

They think it’s, they think it’s really mean when you ask them, “Take out the garbage.” My gosh, you have to leave your Nintendo game for two minutes to take out the garbage. How horrible! But see, that’s what “refresh” means. It means you relieve someone of the burden, you refresh them. And this is what devoted people do. Without the devoted leaders in a church, the other leaders are very limited in what can be done. Are you there? And so devoted leaders are very important. Committed leaders. You can call them subordinate leaders or whatever you want. Paul calls them devoted, committed people. They clean the church, they clean the bathrooms, they do the books, they, you know, they mow the lawn, they, you know, they do things all the time. They visit the sick, they, you know, they encourage people to come to church and they encourage them after service and so forth. Invite them over to their house. These are devoted leaders.

I am glad about the coming of Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus, for what was lacking on your part they supplied. For they refreshed my spirit and yours. Therefore acknowledge such men.

chunks.section_question: How can devoted people help a new Christian?
chunks.short_answer: He says most American Christians are “selfish people” who “don’t know where the hospitality is,” and tells of a couple who “took me under their wing as a young Christian,” fed him, shared the word and called him on Sunday mornings. He says that without them “I don’t know if I would have made it over the hump.”
chunks.text:
Most American Christians are selfish people. They don’t want their basketball game interfered with. “I, leave me alone. I ain’t invite nobody over.” They never invite anybody over. They don’t know where the hospitality is. And the Bible tells us that we are to be what? Hospitable. Am I talking to the right group? Yeah. See, these are devoted people. I tell you, it was those devoted people. I was telling my brother Gary, the [unclear] were a couple back there that took me under their wing as a young Christian and got me through the hump where Satan was trying to say, “Ah, nothing happened. You know, you just, you know, that’s a bunch of [unclear]. You’re not different,” and all the rest. Man, they took me, invited me over their house, and, you know, they fed me, and we sang songs, and they shared the word with me. And they would call me up and said, “Are you coming to church?” And I tell you, I was in bed fast asleep. “Oh yeah, I’m coming.” I wasn’t planning on coming to church, but they called me early Sunday morning: “Are you coming to church today?” “Oh yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah.” Man, I had to get out of that bed and [unclear]. I needed that. They never spoke that I know of, they never preached a message. I never heard one of them prophesy or speak in tongues and interpret or anything else. But let me tell you, without them I don’t know if I would have made it over the hump. I needed those kind of

people. And when I got to their home, they were an example of a Christian. And I love those people, and I tell you, I’m going to greet them heavily when I get to heaven. They were very important to my growth in God. Leadership is important, very important. Don’t think it’s not important where you choose to go to church and the leadership there. Very important. “My people, children are their oppressors.” You know, children are running most homes today. Oh man, we go to little leagues, we go to dance recitals, we, you know, the Americans think that they are going to ingrain character in their kids by all this secular involvement.

chunks.section_question: Are children running American homes, and do sports build character?
chunks.short_answer: He says “children are running most homes today,” and that Americans think they will “ingrain character in their kids” through secular activities. He says that growing up in baseball and football leagues “I didn’t see one kid change,” and that the husband “is one of the most neglected members of the home.”
chunks.text: I grew up in Detroit. I was in those baseball leagues and football leagues and so forth. I didn’t see one kid change. Not one. We just played sports, and when we got done we went back to our neighborhood and dared anybody to bother us. You know it’s true. Children, I mean, the husband in most American homes is one of the most neglected members of the home, because the kids, even though he may work six days a week, the kids just consume their time. Are you out there? Hallelujah, that’s one for the men.

chunks.section_question: What does he say about leading in the home?
chunks.short_answer: He says “if you don’t let Jesus run your life, your woman will,” and that “a good woman wants a good man who’s got control of his life.” To the women he says “you got to be teachable and you got to learn to submit to God’s structure,” and “It’s not your job to make him what he’s supposed to be.”
chunks.text:
“Women rule over them.” Now here’s one, not for the men. Man, if you don’t let Jesus run your life, your woman will. God created us to be men. A good woman wants a good man who’s got control of his life, heading somewhere down the road, following the examples that the Bible says. And if you don’t do it, you’re going to be following your woman, and they’re going to be following their emotions, and I tell you, disaster after disaster comes when that’s set in motions. Hallelujah. Now, for you women looking at me like that, you want me to balance this out? Well, you know, those women can lead too. Yes you can, and you are a leader in the home.

Let me tell you, if you’re going to be a good leader, you got to be teachable, and you got to learn to submit to God’s structure. You got to learn to expect God to make that man what he’s supposed to be. It’s not your job to make him what he’s supposed to be. Boy, that was good. That turns us off. Say, “You be an example. Show us. You don’t be telling us to do things that you’re not doing.” Yeah. Hallelujah. “Oh my people, those who lead you cause you to err and destroy the way of your paths.” Again in Isaiah 9:16, “The leaders of these people cause them to err, and they that are led of them are,” what? Destroyed. Who your leader is is important. Who you’re following, the doctrine. That’s why I tell you, go back to the apostles, go back to Jesus. Like the Berean church. chunks.section_question: Why does it matter who your leader is, and what about false prophets?
chunks.short_answer: He quotes “Many pastors have destroyed my vineyard” and “The prophets prophesy falsely,” and says he hears “a lot of junk” in both Pentecostal and Baptist circles. He says “you’re a self-made prophet” if you are not speaking by the leading of the Holy Ghost, and “you can’t blame leaders only, because that’s what they want to hear.”
chunks.text:
truth. Amen. “Many pastors have destroyed my vineyard,” Jeremiah 12:10. You think leadership isn’t important? Leadership is very important, and having the essentials, and having the skills is very important, and every leader has to start somewhere in their youth and work their way up. Jeremiah 5:31, “The prophets prophesy falsely.” Good Lord, is that ever true, whether it’s in us Pentecostal circles where we believe in prophecy and we have tongues and interpretation, I hear a lot of junk, or whether you are Baptist and you believe prophecy is just an inspired preacher, I hear a lot of junk. How many have heard a lot of junk? How can you be a prophet? Prophecy means spoken by the inspiration of the Holy

Ghost. And if you’re not speaking by the leading of the Holy Ghost, that’s not a, you’re a self-made prophet, you’re not a real one. I don’t care what denomination you’re in. “My people love to have it so.” Here’s the kicker, that’s what the people want to hear. The churches are filling up with preachers that tell them what they want to hear, so you can’t blame leaders only, because that’s what they want to hear. So they find leaders that tell them what they want to hear. But what will you do in the end? What’s the end? The judgment. You got to stand before Christ. What are you going to do? You’re going to say, “Well, I, you know, I followed this guy and he led me astray”? You’re supposed to follow Christ. You’re supposed to follow Paul and Peter and these apostles. You’re not supposed to follow some preacher. He is supposed to follow Christ himself

chunks.section_question: How do I find a good pastor, and is a good leader enough?
chunks.short_answer: He quotes Jeremiah 3:15, “I will give you pastors according to my heart, which will feed you with knowledge and understanding,” and says “They are out there. You need to find them.” He adds that you can have a good leader and still live a wrong life, as King Jotham “did what was right in the sight of the Lord” but “the people still acted corruptly.”
chunks.text: and preach the Scriptures. Amen. Jeremiah 3:15, “I will give you pastors according to my heart, which will feed you with knowledge and understanding.” They are out there. You need to find them. Can I hear an amen? Young believers need to especially find somebody that can teach them the word of God, whether it’s devoted leaders that know the word of God, whether it’s young leaders that know the word of God, or whether it’s skilled leaders that know the word of God. They got to seek out that thing and get under good teaching so they can grow and be strong. Now, you can have a good leader and you can still live a wrong life. 2 Chronicles 27:2, King Jotham “did what was right in the sight of the Lord,” but the people still acted corruptly. They didn’t follow the leader, they did their own thing.

chunks.section_question: Is being a believer enough if I do not follow what the Bible teaches?
chunks.short_answer: He says Paul was a good leader, yet the Corinthians were doing “incest, idols,” and “the choice is yours” whether to follow the Bible’s instructions or “do your own thing.” He says Americans think “because I’m a believer, everything’s okay,” but “faith in being a son of God is not the end of it.”
chunks.text:
Paul’s church growth seminar to the Corinthian church. Was Paul a good leader? Absolutely. Does this letter to the Corinthian church show us they’re following him? No, they’re doing incest, idols. Oh man, they’re doing all kinds of things, and they had a great leader. The bottom line, church, is the choice is yours. You can choose to get a good leader and you can choose to follow the instructions of the Bible that that leader teaches, or you can choose to do your own thing. And what will you do in the end? You got to stand before Christ and give an answer, and you’re going to say, “Well, I’m a believer.” How you think that’s going to go

over? That’s what Americans have us thinking: because I’m a believer, everything’s okay. See, I have eight kids, and all of them believe that I’m their dad, and they know my standards, but that doesn’t make them one that lives right. They have to choose to live right, and so do we. See, faith in being a son of God is not the end of it. Let me show you the power in unity, when the congregation, the young leaders, the devoted leaders, and the skilled leaders get together and become one. chunks.section_question: What is the real problem with the church in America?
chunks.short_answer: He answers “disunity.” He points to Genesis 11:6, where “the people are one,” and 2 Chronicles 5:13, where singers and musicians were “as one in praising and thanking the Lord” and the glory of the Lord filled the house. He says the healing of America is “God’s people getting their act together.”

faqs.question: What does “refresh” mean in this message?
faqs.answer: He says “that’s what refresh means. It means you relieve someone of the burden, you refresh them.” He compares it to someone bringing a cold glass of lemonade to a person plowing, or a son taking over the plow.

scriptures.text_nkjv: I am glad about the coming of Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus, for what was lacking on your part they supplied. For they refreshed my spirit and yours. Therefore acknowledge such men.

faqs.question: What jobs does he say devoted people do in a church?
faqs.answer: He says “they clean the church, they clean the bathrooms, they do the books,” mow the lawn, visit the sick, encourage people to come to church and invite them over to their house.

faqs.question: What does he say about hospitality?
faqs.answer: He says “the Bible tells us that we are to be what? Hospitable,” and that most American Christians “never invite anybody over.”

faqs.question: Did the people who helped him need to preach or prophesy?
faqs.answer: No. He says “They never preached a message. I never heard one of them prophesy or speak in tongues and interpret or anything else,” yet “without them I don’t know if I would have made it over the hump.”

faqs.question: Does he say it matters which church you choose?
faqs.answer: Yes. He says “Don’t think it’s not important where you choose to go to church and the leadership there. Very important.”

faqs.question: Who does he say we are supposed to follow?
faqs.answer: He says “You’re supposed to follow Christ. You’re supposed to follow Paul and Peter and these apostles. You’re not supposed to follow some preacher.” Of the judgment he asks, “what are you going to do?”

scriptures.text_nkjv: The prophets prophesy falsely, And the priests rule by their own power; And My people love to have it so. But what will you do in the end?

faqs.question: What does he say about preachers who tell people what they want to hear?
faqs.answer: He says “The churches are filling up with preachers that tell them what they want to hear, so you can’t blame leaders only, because that’s what they want to hear.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: The prophets prophesy falsely, And the priests rule by their own power; And My people love to have it so. But what will you do in the end?

faqs.question: What does he say his own children show about faith?
faqs.answer: He says “I have eight kids, and all of them believe that I’m their dad, and they know my standards, but that doesn’t make them one that lives right. They have to choose to live right, and so do we.”

faqs.question: What does he say is the source of healing for America?
faqs.answer: He asks whether it is the Democrats or Republicans, or the rich people or the poor people, and answers no each time: “It’s God’s people getting their act together.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: if My people who are called by My name will humble themselves, and pray and seek My face, and turn from their wicked ways, then I will hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin and heal their land.

faqs.question: What does he say about Protestants and the idea of hell?
faqs.answer: He says “Nobody in the Protestant church feels like they’re going to hell,” and that at funerals nobody says someone is going there: “We all live in this delusion.”

faqs.question: Why does he say Jesus died on the cross?
faqs.answer: He says “That’s why he died on the cross, to change the way you acted toward other people,” and “to forgive you of hating other people and mistreating other people.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: For all the law is fulfilled in one word, even in this: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.”

faqs.question: What does he say about psychology in the church?
faqs.answer: He says “Psychology has crept into the church. It’s horrible. Nowhere did Christ preach psychology.”

faqs.question: What does he say about children and parents?
faqs.answer: He says “Our children supposed to honor their parents,” and parents are supposed to raise their children up “in the nurture and admonition of the Lord” and be an example.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right. “Honor your father and mother,” which is the first commandment with promise: “that it may be well with you and you may live long on the earth.” And you, fathers, do not provoke your children to wrath, but bring them up in the training and admonition of the Lord.

faqs.question: What is the greatest thing you can give your child?
faqs.answer: He asks, “What’s the greatest thing you can give your kid?” and answers “Seeing you guys enjoying one another.”
